data.gender_notes: Ashvini is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Ashvini are the twin horse deities of the moon. They are associated with healing, fertility, and good fortune. The name Ashvini carries the meaning “Horse” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashvini usually hope their child will grow to embody horse and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ashvini belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Horse.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashvini total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The Ashvini Kumaras are the twin physicians and attendants of the moon, Chandra. They are mentioned in numerous Hindu sacred texts, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas. They are considered to be the removers of suffering, givers of health and happiness, and the bestowers of immortality.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the Ashvini Kumaras are seen as symbolizing the healing power of the divine and the interconnectedness of all living beings. They represent the idea that suffering and pain are temporary and can be healed through faith, devotion, and the grace of the divine.

historical_references.reference: The Ashvini Kumaras are believed to be the divine physicians and healers in Hindu mythology. They are also identified with the stars of the constellation of the Ascendant (Lagna), known as the 'Ashvini Stars'. Some believe they are the twin horses of the Sun God, Surya, and are Kartikeya's attendants.

In the Rigveda, one of the oldest Hindu scriptures, the Ashvini twins are referred to as the dispellers of sickness and sorrow. They are also mentioned as the first to perform the sacrificial rites, which indicates their role as priests and spiritual leaders.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ashvini is derived from Hindu mythology and is associated with the Ashvini Kumaras, twin divine horse-riding physicians. In modern context, the name Ashvini is popularly used in various spheres such as Ayurvedic medicine, astrology, and Hindu mythology.
